transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t get past this feeling that I’m a danger to people and a disappointment. There was a near-miss, and I keep thinking that proves I’m not meant to be a nurse. It feels like everyone would be better off without me around.
Have you been having thoughts of killing yourself?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But… yeah, I’ve been having thoughts like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. I used to do little things to clear my head—go jogging, knit, cook something, read after class. Now I just… don’t. I’ll sit on my bed still in my scrubs and I can’t make myself care about any of it.
Did these feelings start after the near-miss at work?

Not exactly. The near-miss made it feel a lot worse, but this has been going on for about a year and a couple months—since after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic.
Lately, have you been having trouble taking care of basic things like showering, eating regular meals, or getting to work or class?

Yeah… I’ve been falling behind in my nursing prereq classes, and at work I’m not handling things the way I used to. I keep needing coworkers to double-check tasks I used to feel sure about. It makes me scared to take on normal clinic responsibilities.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or drained most days?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I feel worn out a lot, but I haven’t been keeping track of whether it’s most days.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. At night I just lie there going over charts and med calculations in my head, like replaying everything. And when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up before my alarm already exhausted and scared I missed something.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?

Yeah. Most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Even when I’m smiling at patients in Spanish or trying to seem normal at the clinic, I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.
Do you feel worthless or blame yourself a lot for what’s been happening?

Yes. I blame myself a lot. I keep thinking that near-miss means I’m not supposed to be a nurse, like I’m dangerous or a disappointment. It’s hard to shake the feeling that everyone would be better off without me there.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. My brain feels really foggy. I’ll read the same medication order or even a lecture slide over and over and still not take it in. And sometimes I get stuck on small decisions, like what to chart first, and I just freeze for a bit.
For at least two weeks, have you felt this down nearly every day?

Yes. It’s been nearly every day for way longer than two weeks—about a year and two months now. It started after I graduated high school and began college classes while working full-time at the clinic.
If the near-miss had never happened, do you think you would still be feeling this depressed?

I think… yes, I probably would. The near-miss made it worse, but most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest anyway. Even when I’m smiling at patients in Spanish or trying to act normal at the clinic, I feel like I’m just barely holding myself together.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yes. I don’t really get hungry much, and I’ll forget to eat until late in the day. Then I might just force down some crackers or have coffee. My work pants have been getting looser, but I’m not trying to lose weight.
Do you truly believe you are dangerous to other people?

I don’t think I’d ever hurt someone on purpose. But I can’t stop feeling like I’m a danger anyway, like that near-miss proves I shouldn’t be a nurse. I feel like a disappointment… like people would be better off without me around.
Have other people noticed that you've been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?
Yes. A few people at the clinic have asked me if I’m tired. I guess I’ve been moving slower when I’m getting supplies, and sometimes even with simple questions, it takes me a few seconds to answer.
Do you believe, with certainty, that people really would be better off without you?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m certain, but it feels true a lot of the time. Since that near-miss, I keep thinking it proves I’m not meant to be a nurse, and that I’m a danger and a disappointment. Then my mind goes to, maybe everyone would be better off without me.
